missing_evidence: No production server path consumes realtime.wsTransportMode or parseWsTransportRequest, and no production browser path opens or manages split control/output sockets.
No default test command executes the standalone split server suites; frontend/package.json also has no general unit-test command covering all tests.

No deterministic characterization contract or runner defines NO_RENDER, NO_ANALYZER, NO_NETWORK, or ONE_CLIENT_SLOW workloads, warm-up, iterations, raw samples, output schema, or repeatability tolerance.
No multi-client test proves that one slow client cannot delay, reorder, duplicate, or disconnect a normal client receiving the same session stream.
No actual-upgrade integration test traverses HTTPS upgrade parsing, authentication, split pairing, browser URL construction, fallback, and reconnection together.

No regression injects a screen-repair frame during the WebSocketContext remount grace gap; current code skips that frame, while server timeout only releases queued output and does not reissue the lost repair.
No full retained-state equivalence evidence exists: server and browser recovery are explicitly viewport-only, and the authority E2E positively verifies that older scrollback is absent.
No deterministic evidence quantifies the data-loss boundary of oversized empty fallback when the browser has no valid local viewport snapshot and displays only the fallback placeholder.

Telemetry configuration fields sampleIntervalMs and recentEventLimit are not wired into a characterization sampler/artifact writer; existing observations are cumulative snapshots and fixed in-memory limits.
Existing numeric caps and timing constants lack workload-derived confidence intervals or threshold justification and therefore cannot be promoted from characterization seeds to product targets.
